title: A Dolphin Swims Through a Flooded Forest by Bending Its Neck 90 Degrees

scenes.text: A dolphin swims through the treetops of a flooded forest.
It's the Amazon river dolphin, the boto. Every year the rivers overflow, flooding thousands of square miles of rainforest.
The flood lasts about half the year. And this dolphin is up to eight feet long and 450 pounds.
That should get it stuck in the branches. But its neck bones aren't fused, so it bends its head up to ninety degrees.
It threads between trunks the way you'd weave through a crowd.
A body built for open water, with a neck built for a forest.

description:
A dolphin swims through the treetops of a flooded forest.
The Amazon river dolphin has unfused neck bones that let it bend its head up to 90 degrees, so it can weave between flooded trees.
Would you swim with a pink dolphin? Comment below.
first_comment: Male botos can turn pink, probably from scarring. Did you know that, or did you think they were born pink?
